epithet: He does not speak from his own desire
lede: The first surah the Prophet ﷺ recited aloud to a gathering of Quraysh. It tells what he saw, and how certain it was; sets against it the three goddesses of Makkah, which were names and nothing more; and ends on a command so compelling that everyone present — believer and idolater alike — went down in prostration.

names.name: al-Najm
names.note: After the oath it opens with: by the star when it sets. Ibn Masʿūd refers to it as Wa-l-najm (al-Bukhārī 4863).

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records agreement that it is Makkan, with one ayah (53:32) excepted in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah. He also relates Muqātil’s remark that this is the first surah the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proclaimed openly in Makkah — and Ibn Masʿūd, in al-Bukhārī, says it was the first surah to be sent down containing a prostration. The traditional order places it twenty-third.
revelation.when: Makkah — the first surah recited publicly at the Kaʿbah

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ النَّجْمِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ إلّا أنَّهُ قَدْ حُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةَ أنَّهُما قالا: إلّا آيَةً مِنها
وهَذِهِ أوَّلُ سُورَةٍ أعْلَنَها رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ

setting: For some years the Qurʾan had been recited in houses and in the hills. Then, one day at the Kaʿbah, with the men of Quraysh sitting in their circles, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and recited this surah to them from beginning to end.

It begins by vouching for him. “Your companion has not gone astray, nor has he erred, nor does he speak out of desire: it is nothing but a revelation revealed.” Then it tells them what he has seen. One mighty in power taught him — Jibrīl — who stood on the highest horizon in his true form, then drew near, to within two bows’ length or nearer. And he saw him a second time, on the night he was taken up, by the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge. ʿĀʾishah explained these ayat: it was Jibrīl; he saw him in the form in which he was created only these two times. Ibn Masʿūd said: he saw Jibrīl with six hundred wings.

Having said what he saw, the surah turns to what they worship. “Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other?” — the three goddesses whose shrines stood within a few days’ ride of Makkah, and whom Quraysh called the daughters of Allah. “They are nothing but names that you have named, you and your fathers.”

Its last words are a command: “So prostrate to Allah, and worship.” Ibn Masʿūd says that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, and everyone behind him prostrated — except one man, whom he saw take a handful of dust, raise it to his forehead and say, “This is enough for me.” “Afterwards I saw him killed as a disbeliever.” Ibn ʿAbbās adds that the Muslims and the idolaters, the jinn and the humans, all prostrated.
aim: To establish the truthfulness of the revelation and the loftiness of its source — affirming the creed of tawḥīd, and overturning the creed of shirk.
themes: The Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary

outline.title: What he saw
outline.summary: By the star when it sets: your companion has not strayed, nor does he speak from desire; it is only revelation revealed, taught him by one mighty in power. He stood on the highest horizon, then drew near, two bows’ length or nearer. The heart did not belie what it saw. And he saw him at another descent, by the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, near the Garden of Refuge. The sight did not swerve, nor did it overstep. He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.

outline.title: The three goddesses
outline.summary: Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other? Are yours the males, and His the females? That would be an unjust division. They are only names that you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority for them. They follow nothing but conjecture and what their souls desire.

outline.title: Intercession, and His knowledge of you
outline.summary: How many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing, except after Allah gives leave to whom He wills. So turn from the one who turns from Our remembrance and wants only the life of this world. Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, apart from small faults — your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knew you when He produced you from the earth and when you were hidden in your mothers’ wombs: so do not claim purity for yourselves.

outline.title: What is in the scriptures of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm
outline.summary: Have you seen the one who turned away, gave a little and then stopped? Has he not been told what is in the scrolls of Mūsā, and of Ibrāhīm who fulfilled his charge: that no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another; that man has only what he strives for; that his striving will be seen; and then he will be repaid for it in full?

outline.title: To your Lord is the end
outline.summary: To your Lord is the final end. It is He who makes to laugh and to weep, who gives death and life, who created the pair, male and female; upon Him is the second creation; He enriches and contents; He is the Lord of Sirius. He destroyed the first ʿĀd, and Thamūd, and the people of Nūḥ before, and overthrew the ruined cities. Then which of your Lord’s favours will you doubt?

outline.title: The Approaching draws near
outline.summary: This is a warner, of the warners of old. The Approaching has drawn near; none besides Allah can unveil it. Do you then wonder at this discourse, and laugh and not weep, lost in your amusements? So prostrate to Allah, and worship.

keyAyah.why: With the ayah after it, the Qurʾan’s own statement about the one who delivered it — and the foundation on which the Sunnah stands.

virtues.text: “The first surah to be sent down in which there is a prostration was al-Najm. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, and those behind him prostrated — except a man whom I saw take a handful of dust and prostrate on it. Afterwards I saw him killed as a disbeliever: he was Umayyah ibn Khalaf.”
“The Prophet ﷺ prostrated at al-Najm, and with him prostrated the Muslims and the idolaters, the jinn and mankind.”
On “two bows’ length or nearer; and He revealed to His servant what He revealed”: Ibn Masʿūd said that he ﷺ saw Jibrīl, who had six hundred wings.

virtuesNote: The story told in some books to explain why the idolaters prostrated — that words in praise of their goddesses were cast into the recitation — has no sound chain. Ibn Kathīr says of its routes, at the place in Sūrat al-Ḥajj where it is cited, that they are all disconnected and that he has not seen it with a sound, connected chain.
before: Al-Ṭūr closed with glorification at the setting of the stars. Al-Najm opens: by the star when it sets.
after: Al-Najm ends: the Approaching has drawn near. Al-Qamar begins: the Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.
